pages.title: Foreword
pages.text: Whoever finds this journal: I was an alchemist. I chased the old dream, one matter into another, and failed like everyone before me. Until the night I tore reality.$(br2)This is how I learned to use the tear. Read it in order.

pages.title: The Tear
pages.text: It began with lapis and amethyst. Burned together in a sealed room, the lapis did not turn to ash. It turned to $(thing)distortion$(), a pressure that bent the walls and the light in them. Stone flowed. Glass forgot it was glass.

pages.title: The Leak
pages.text: But the power ran wild. It spilled out of every crack, and when the fire died it was gone.$(br2)I had opened a door, and could keep nothing that came through.

pages.title: The Cycle
pages.text: What I wanted never changed. Ores $(l:machines/destructuration)broken$() into pure $(l:basics/compounds)compounds$(), compounds $(l:machines/transmutation)transmuted$() into other matter, the result $(l:machines/reconstruction)rebuilt$() into ores and ingots. The alchemical cycle.$(br2)Every step would run on $(thing)distortion energy$(), which I came to count in DE.

pages.title: Chambers
pages.text: Every machine I built is a $(thing)chamber$(), ordinary blocks around a $(item)core$(), remade by it the moment the structure is right.$(br2)$(#FF7F9A)Break any part and the frame collapses with nothing left.$() Only the core survives. I lost three workshops learning that.

pages.title: This Journal
pages.text: I bound a little distortion into these pages. Ask a machine's page to $(thing)Visualize$() and look where it should stand, and its blocks will wait there as ghosts.$(br2)Touch a core, or any stone of its frame, and the machine opens to you. Hold a block instead, and you will simply lay it down.
